s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive visual impairment with night blindness and scotomas
salient_findings: Inferonasal scotoma on Goldmann visual field
Abnormal electroretinogram with flat rod response
Inner retinal thickening and disorganization on OCT
key_facts: Patient age 42
Symptoms started in childhood
Night blindness is the only symptom reported
Visual acuity 20/25 to 20/30 in both eyes
Color vision is normal
Fundus examination shows few yellow spots and indistinct grayish circle
Electroretinogram shows large, slow scotopic and photopic responses
Rod electroretinogram is flat
Lower ERG amplitudes compared to 30 years ago
Fundus autofluorescence shows hypofluorescence in superotemporal zones
OCT shows supernormal thickness in perifoveal region
OCT shows marked inner retinal thickening and disorganization in eccentric areas
Complete loss of photoreceptors, ellipsoid zone, and retinal pigment epithelium in superotemporal region

shortlist.label: Retinitis pigmentosa
shortlist.why_kept: Night blindness since childhood, flat rod electroretinogram, and characteristic fundus findings

shortlist.label: Choroideremia
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive visual impairment with night blindness, and fundus autofluorescence showing hypofluorescence in superotemporal zones

shortlist.label: Gyrate atrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Night blindness, and OCT showing marked inner retinal thickening and disorganization in eccentric areas

shortlist.label: Leber congenital amaurosis
shortlist.why_kept: Night blindness since childhood, and severe retinal dysfunction on electroretinogram

shortlist.label: Cone-rod dystrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive visual impairment with night blindness, and OCT showing supernormal thickness in perifoveal region

raw.rationale: The patient's lifelong history of night blindness without significant progression or other visual symptoms, combined with normal color vision and relatively preserved visual acuity, supports this diagnosis. The electroretinogram showing a flat rod response is also consistent with Congenital Stationary Night Blindness.

rejected.label: Retinitis Pigmentosa
rejected.why: Typically progresses to significant visual field loss and often affects visual acuity and color vision over time, which is not seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Choroideremia
rejected.why: Characterized by progressive loss of the choroid, retinal pigment epithelium, and photoreceptors, leading to more severe visual impairment than described.

rejected.label: Oguchi Disease
rejected.why: Often presents with a distinctive golden-yellow sheen in the retina and typically improves with light adaptation, which is not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Stargardt Disease
rejected.why: Typically presents with progressive bilateral atrophy of the macular areas and significant visual acuity loss, which is not consistent with this patient's relatively preserved visual acuity and normal color vision.
